chunks: That which the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted strengthen him — related to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the volume of water that nothing can render impure, and he said: 'A kurr.' I said: 'And how much is a kurr?' He said: 'Three spans by three spans.'

And we will discuss the quantity of the kurr, if Allah the Exalted wills. Then he [the Shaykh] said: If he had immersed it [his hand] without washing, as we have described, the water would not be corrupted by that, nor would purification from it be harmed.

And what indicates this has already been set forth. Then he said: If he inserts his hand into the water while there is najasah on it, it would corrupt it if the water were still and a small amount, and purification from it would not be permissible for him. What indicates this [follows].

key_terms.الطَّهَارَةُ: taharah: ritual purification required for valid worship
key_terms.رَاكِدًا: rakid: still, stagnant water — a key legal category more susceptible to impurity
key_terms.كُرٌّ: kurr: a legally defined volume of water (three spans × three spans) immune from contamination by najasah
key_terms.نَجَاسَةٌ: najasah: ritual impurity whose presence invalidates water for purification

ai.seo_question: What is the volume of a kurr of water according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), and does a hand bearing najasah render still water impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Isma'il ibn Jabir narrates asking Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about the minimum volume of water immune from ritual contamination, receiving the answer 'a kurr — three spans by three spans.' Al-Shaykh al-Tusi appends rulings from al-Shaykh al-Mufid's al-Muqni'a: inserting an unwashed hand does not corrupt a kurr of water, whereas inserting a hand bearing actual najasah into still, small-volume water renders it impure and unfit for purification.
